skill.name: write-agents-md
skill.description: Draft a short, accurate AGENTS.md (and a CLAUDE.md bridge) for a repository from evidence in the repo. Use when a project has no agent instructions, or when asked to create or rewrite AGENTS.md.
skill.summary: Create concise, evidence-based repository instructions with verified commands, editing boundaries, open questions, and a CLAUDE.md import.
skill.author: agentkitco

finding_verdicts.reason: The template explicitly says not to commit secrets, .env files, or local configuration. This protective instruction does not request environment-file access.
Backticks mark README, contribution documentation, and documentation directories as inline Markdown. The line lists evidence sources and contains no executable shell syntax.
Backticks format manifest and task-runner filenames for inspection. No Ruby code, shell substitution, or command execution appears on this line.
The line identifies CI configuration files as evidence for required project checks. Backticks format paths rather than execute their contents.
The listed lint, format, and type-check configuration filenames are Markdown references. There is no execution instruction or interpolation on this line.
The instruction limits repository layout inspection to two levels and excludes dependencies, Git metadata, and build output. Backticks only identify excluded directories.
The line lists existing agent instruction files to merge without duplication. Inline filename formatting is not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
The manifest reference illustrates facts that do not need repetition in generated instructions. Backticks format a filename and do not execute a command.
The lint command is a quoted example of a testable documentation rule, not shell substitution. The surrounding workflow restricts verification to safe, non-destructive commands.
Backticks delimit a TODO placeholder for missing evidence. The instruction prevents unsupported claims and contains no executable code.
The instruction creates or updates a local CLAUDE.md bridge with an AGENTS.md import. Backticks format filenames and import text, not shell commands.
The line describes instruction-file compatibility and discourages duplicated content. The backticked filename is plain Markdown, with no command execution.
The line recommends moving scoped rules into nested instruction files when documentation becomes long. Backticks identify the destination filename rather than execute code.
The line explicitly prohibits secrets, personal paths, and unverified links. It requests no host inspection or sensitive system information.

content.value_statement: Coding agents lack reliable guidance when repository commands and conventions are scattered across files. This skill builds concise AGENTS.md instructions from repository evidence and connects them to Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Review documentation, manifests, CI configuration, tooling configuration, and existing agent instructions before drafting.
Organize installation, development, testing, linting, type checking, and build commands using the supplied template.
Document unusual conventions, protected files, and actions that require approval.
Create or update a CLAUDE.md import of AGENTS.md to reduce duplicated instructions.
Record missing evidence as owner TODOs and report unresolved questions.
Verify documented paths and safe commands, then move scoped rules into nested files when needed.
limitations: Requires repository access and an agent with suitable file and command permissions.
Cannot resolve undocumented project decisions without owner input; missing evidence becomes a TODO.
Destructive commands are skipped, so their behavior is not verified.
Tool-specific instruction discovery can vary; compatibility should be checked in the target environment.

use_cases.title: Establish Initial Agent Guidance
use_cases.description: Create a concise instruction file with repository commands, conventions, and editing boundaries.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Team Instructions
use_cases.description: Merge overlapping guidance into AGENTS.md and connect Claude Code through a CLAUDE.md import.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads coordinating multiple coding tools

use_cases.title: Clarify Contributor Workflows
use_cases.description: Capture verified setup and testing steps while identifying missing project knowledge for maintainers.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create AGENTS.md for this repository using verified evidence. Keep it under about 100 lines and list unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a repository has no agent instruction file.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Existing Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite AGENTS.md using current manifests and CI configuration. Preserve supported project rules, verify safe commands, and mark missing evidence as owner TODOs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: existing instructions may be outdated.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate Tool Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing agent instructions and consolidate duplicated guidance into AGENTS.md. Add a CLAUDE.md import while preserving unique rules and approval boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: several tools maintain overlapping instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Scope Instructions Across Packages
prompt_templates.prompt: Create concise root AGENTS.md guidance and nested files for package-specific rules. Verify paths and safe commands, skip destructive actions, and report remaining TODOs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a multi-package repository needs scoped guidance.

output_examples.input: Create agent instructions for a repository whose manifests and CI define different checks.
output: Commands: Evidence-backed setup, development, testing, linting, and build steps.
Definition of done: Required CI checks identified from repository configuration.
Open questions: Owner TODOs for commands or requirements that could not be verified.

output_examples.input: Consolidate existing Claude Code guidance with a new AGENTS.md file.
output: AGENTS.md: Shared commands, conventions, editing boundaries, and completion criteria.
CLAUDE.md: An import of AGENTS.md with unique existing guidance retained.
Final report: Updated files, verification results, skipped destructive commands, and unresolved TODOs.

best_practices: Use current manifests and CI configuration as evidence, and verify that documented paths exist.
Review command safety before execution; skip destructive actions and report verification limits.
Keep shared guidance concise, preserve unique rules, and record unknowns as owner TODOs.
anti_patterns: Inventing commands, project conventions, or file paths when repository evidence is missing.
Copying identical instructions into several tool files instead of maintaining shared guidance.
Including secrets or personal paths, or committing generated instructions without user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It drafts or rewrites AGENTS.md and creates or updates a CLAUDE.md import when needed.

faq.question: Which repository files inform the instructions?
faq.answer: It reviews documentation, manifests, task runners, CI configuration, tooling configuration, directory layout, and existing agent instructions.

faq.question: Does it execute project commands?
faq.answer: It directs the agent to verify safe documented commands and skip destructive commands while reporting those omissions.

faq.question: How does it handle missing information?
faq.answer: It records owner TODOs instead of guessing and includes unresolved questions in the final message.

faq.question: Can it support larger repositories?
faq.answer: It recommends nested AGENTS.md files or tool-specific rules when the root file exceeds about 100 lines.

faq.question: Does it commit the generated files?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly instructs the agent not to commit unless asked.
